# A swap-symmetric assignment singles out no role

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`a-swap-symmetric-assignment-singles-out-none` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F01 · [record](a-swap-symmetric-assignment-singles-out-none.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> Exchanging two roles keeps no predicate that holds of exactly one of them, while each of the two single assignments holds of exactly one: an assignment singling out one of two roles is not kept by their exchange.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. A predicate on two roles, read as the two Boolean values, that holds of each role exactly where it holds of the other does not hold of exactly one of them; the assignment to the first role and the assignment to the second each hold of exactly one, so each fits a task needing exactly one. (`PracticalPriorityIdentification.SwapInvariant`, `PracticalPriorityIdentification.ExactlyOne`, `PracticalPriorityIdentification.symmetric_assignment_not_unique`, `PracticalPriorityIdentification.two_assignments_fit_one_task`)
   - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* not measured: none of its declarations is in the spine run the measure reads.

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- Empty axiom reports for the cited declarations; the module imports Lean's Std and stands off the spine.
- Two roles, read as the two Boolean values; that the assignment is kept by the exchange, and that the task needs exactly one role, are supplied.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- What warrant an asymmetry or a procedure singling out one role has, or which role ought to contribute.
- That actual parties are exactly symmetric: a real asymmetry in undertaking or control fails the premise.
- More than two roles, or symmetries other than the exchange of the two.

<a id="correspondence--对应"></a>
### Correspondence

Social choice: the anonymity and neutrality conditions of May (1952), under which a rule treating voters alike and the two alternatives alike picks neither where the votes are evenly split; read by the AI, the focal points of Schelling (1960) and the correlation devices of Aumann (1974) are the asymmetries that coordination on one of two symmetric roles needs.
